conviction_note: FY26 (to 30 Sep) is effectively pre-released (Q4 AUM of £20.0bn on 13 Oct with 'expectations unchanged', and a £109-113m revenue range given in April), so the move sits in lines nobody has seen: the FY27 cost response to a revenue run-rate about 14% below FY26, the final dividend under the 55%-of-adjusted-PAT policy, any new buyback, and October-November flows. The fact-based sum (-0.9) and the scaled number (-0.15) agree in sign and differ in size because p_up sits near 50: the bar is unsourced, the sign of the FY27 guide is a guess, and a name 26% down over 60 days with shorts building could go either way. The size is large (7.5%) because this AIM name has moved -10.0%, -14.7%, +8.3%, +5.6% on recent results days and -9.4% on its Q4 AUM update.

already_public.what: Q4 AUM update: AUM £20.0bn at 30 Sep 2026 (from £23.3bn at 30 Jun), Q4 net outflows £2.39bn, FY26 net outflows £7.78bn; 'Management expectations for this financial year remain unchanged.' Stock fell 9.4% that day (101.4p to 91.9p, Yahoo tape)

Interim results: H1 revenue £58.8m, adj operating profit £11.3m (19.2% margin), adj diluted EPS 7.4p, interim dividend cut to 2.0p from 4.0p, cash £46.0m, capital surplus £49.1m, dividend policy 'at least 55% of adjusted profit after tax' 'in normal circumstances', ~30 role cost cut
FY26 revenue range of £109m-£113m quoted by the company alongside the loss of most of the £894m Impax Environmental Markets trust; shares -25% that day
Notice of Results: finals for the year to 30 Sep 2026 on Wednesday 25 Nov 2026, analyst meeting 08:30, presentation on website from 07:30

new_in_release.expect: First commentary on FY27 (Impax gives no formal EPS guide but gave a revenue range last April). On the exit AUM of £20.0bn the revenue run-rate is about £98m against an H1 cost run-rate near £95m annualised, so the cost response decides it. More cuts would be positive, holding costs flat to invest would be negative. Direction unknown, magnitude large.

If the policy holds, a final of about 5p (FY adj EPS about 13-14p x 55% = about 7.4p, less the 2.0p interim). There is a risk of a cut below policy, since the policy only applies 'in normal circumstances' and the FY27 run-rate is weak. Slight downside skew against the policy arithmetic.

Possible AUM or flow commentary for Oct-Nov 2026. Management said in October it expects own flows to improve as performance track records strengthen, but Q4 outflows (£2.39bn) accelerated from Q3 (about £1.75bn). Unknown.
Capital allocation: possibly a second buyback given cash of about £46m and a £49.1m capital surplus against a market cap of about £102m. Not signalled, so this is an upside candidate only.
FY26 revenue likely about £113m, at the top of the £109-113m range (H1 £58.8m plus H2 at about 2.45m per £bn of average AUM). Within guidance, so no move expected on this line.

findings.finding: FY26 revenue is pre-guided at £109-113m and 'expectations unchanged' was reiterated on 13 Oct; arithmetic from the H1 revenue and the quarterly AUM path puts it at about £113m, the top of the range. The reported year is therefore already known.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY25 finals (1 Dec 2025) on a pre-released AUM year fell 10.0% over the window (7% by 10:00 per Alliance/HL); the move came from the dividend cut and outflow tone, not the reported revenue
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. The company gave both the range and the reiteration, the stock fell 9.4% on the Q4 update, and it is filed at 0 on that basis.

findings.finding: FY27 starts from AUM of £20.0bn, about 17% below the H1 FY26 average (about £24bn). At H1's fee yield (about 49bp) that is a revenue run-rate of about £98m against H1 operating costs of £47.5m (about £95m annualised), so without further cuts the FY27 adjusted margin falls to low single digits. The cost and FY27 commentary in this release is the line that moves the stock.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interims May 2024 -14.7% and finals Dec 2025 -10.0% came on outflow/outlook disappointment; interims May 2025 +8.3% came on stabilisation; the April 2026 trust-loss update with the revenue range -25%
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The exit AUM has been public since 13 Oct and the stock is down 26% over 60 days, so analysts can do this arithmetic. What is not public is management's cost answer. If the market had fully discounted a margin collapse with no response, a cost-cut announcement would be the dominant surprise. The sign is negative only because the period's own trend (Q4 outflows accelerating) argues against the improvement management keeps forecasting. The bar is unsourced, so this is capped small.
findings.independence: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/impax-asset-management-group--ipx/q4-aum-update/9819119 (the exit AUM and the Q4 acceleration, the same company but a separate document)

findings.finding: The dividend policy is 'at least 55% of adjusted profit after tax' 'in normal circumstances'. With H1 adj EPS of 7.4p and H2 likely lower, the policy-implied FY total is about 7p and the final about 5p, roughly 6% of the 80p spot. A board facing a weak FY27 run-rate could pay below the policy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The final dividend cut to 8.0p from 22.9p (in line with policy) came with a -10.0% day in Dec 2025; the halved interim (2.0p) came with a +0.6% day in May 2026
findings.why_not_priced: The policy is public, so a policy-consistent final is priced. The unpriced part is a departure from the policy, and the 'normal circumstances' qualifier gives the board the room. If the market expected a sub-policy cut, the stock would trade at an implied yield well above 9% on the policy arithmetic, which it does; that is consistent with partial pricing of a cut. Sized near 0 because it lands inside the stated policy.
findings.independence: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/impax-asset-management-group--ipx/final-results/9265936 (FY25: 12.0p total = 55.7% of adj PAT, 'in line with stated policy', so the board followed the policy last time)

findings.finding: The balance sheet against the market value: cash of £46.0m and a capital surplus of £49.1m at 31 Mar 2026 against a market cap of about £102m (127.0m shares at 80.4p). The company completed a first £10m buyback at an average of 180p in Dec 2025 under its 'focus on effective capital allocation', so a second buyback or capital return is a live candidate for the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback was announced in May 2025 alongside interims, a +8.3% day (with stabilising flows in the same release)
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing has signalled a new buyback (there are no Transaction in Own Shares RNS since Dec 2025 on Investegate), so an announcement would be new. This is an inference: cash will have fallen through H2 with the interim dividend and EBT purchases, and the board may prefer to defend the dividend. Hence small, with a positive-only range.
findings.independence: https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/IPX (no buyback RNS since 22 Dec 2025 completion)
